<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="שבט_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518916658_theRebbe_485" batchId="meluket-_D7_A9_D7_91_D7_98_meluket__BH_POST_1766518916658_theRebbe_485__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section contains the heading and date of the maamar.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">B”H,</t>
    <t s="1">10 Shevat,</t>
    <t s="2">5713*</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the Shechinah originally dwelt in the lower realms, was removed due to sin, and was drawn back down by the righteous, especially through the service of subjugating the sitra achra, which is connected to the wood of the shittim tree representing "folly" in holiness.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">“I have come to My garden,</t>
    <t s="1">My sister, [My] bride.”¹</t>
    <t s="2">And it is brought in the Midrash Rabbah</t>
    <t s="3">(in its place²):</t>
    <t s="4">“To My garden, to My bridal chamber, to the place which was My primary [dwelling] initially.”</t>
    <t s="5">For the primary dwelling of the Shechinah was in the lower realms.</t>
    <t s="6">And through the sin of the Tree of Knowledge and the sins that followed it, they removed the Shechinah from below to above, up to the seventh firmament.</t>
    <t s="7">And the righteous who came afterwards, until Moshe Rabbeinu,</t>
    <t s="8">who is the seventh, and all sevenths are beloved,³</t>
    <t s="9">drew down the Shechinah from above to below, even into the actual physical land.</t>
    <t s="10">And regarding this drawing down, it is stated⁴</t>
    <t s="11">“And they shall make Me a Sanctuary, and I will dwell in their midst.”</t>
    <t s="12">It does not say “in its midst,” but rather “in their midst,”</t>
    <t s="13">within each and every one of Israel.⁵</t>
    <t s="14">And this means that through the righteous doing all the matters themselves and effecting this in the people of their generation</t>
    <t s="15">(they carry out the matters themselves and effect this in the generation),</t>
    <t s="16">through this they draw down the Shechinah into the lower realms as it was initially.</t>
    <t s="17">And even more—that they also draw down the essence of the Shechinah into the lower realms,</t>
    <t s="18">as is explained in the maamar⁶</t>
    <t s="19">“The day of histalkus and the day of yahrtzeit,” in the explanation of the maamar of the Zohar,⁷</t>
    <t s="20">“When the sitra achra is subdued, the glory of the Holy One, blessed be He, is elevated throughout all worlds.”</t>
    <t s="21">For its explanation is the light that shines equally in all worlds,</t>
    <t s="22">and the drawing down is through the service of subjugating the sitra achra,</t>
    <t s="23">which in the services of the Holy Temple is the service of the offerings, and specifically the act of the incense offering.⁸</t>
    <t s="24">And this is also the reason⁸</t>
    <t s="25">why the Mishkan was made specifically</t>
    <t s="26">from shittim wood.⁹</t>
    <t s="27">For, behold,¹⁰</t>
    <t s="28">“shittah” means “deviation,” and it also means “folly.”¹¹</t>
    <t s="29">That is, there is a thing that is intermediate,</t>
    <t s="30">and the deviation to one side,</t>
    <t s="31">upward or downward,</t>
    <t s="32">is called “shittah.”</t>
    <t s="33">For the deviation upward is the folly of holiness, and the deviation downward is the folly of the opposite side.</t>
    <t s="34">The way of the Torah and mitzvos in general</t>
    <t s="35">is the middle path, as the Rambam writes in Hilchos Deos.¹²</t>
    <t s="36">And the deviation upward from the middle path is the folly of holiness,</t>
    <t s="37">for there must also be the folly of holiness,</t>
    <t s="38">and specifically when one must be careful</t>
    <t s="39">(to guard)</t>
    <t s="40">that the folly of the opposite side should not occur,</t>
    <t s="41">it is specifically through the folly of holiness,</t>
    <t s="42">as per the statement¹³</t>
    <t s="43">“His folly benefited the old man,”</t>
    <t s="44">that the folly of holiness benefits and rectifies the folly of the opposite side.</t>
    <t s="45">And as it is stated regarding the future to come, “And he will water the Brook of Shittim,”¹⁴</t>
    <t s="46">through which “the glory of the Holy One, blessed be He, will be elevated throughout all worlds.”</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that a Jew cannot sin from his own essence, and only a spirit of folly that obscures the truth can cause him to sin, making him worse than the sitra achra and even a mosquito.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">ב)</t>
    <t s="1">And now,¹⁰ to understand the general concept of the folly of the opposite side, because of which the folly of holiness is necessary, and through this “the glory of the Holy One, blessed be He, is elevated throughout all worlds,”</t>
    <t s="2">behold, it is written,¹⁵</t>
    <t s="3">“When a man’s wife goes astray [tishteh],” and Rashi explains: “deviates from the ways of modesty.”</t>
    <t s="4">And it is written,¹⁶</t>
    <t s="5">“And Israel dwelt in Shittim,” and it is brought in the Midrash,</t>
    <t s="6">that Shittim is a place that causes folly, through which they come to transgression of licentiousness. And as our Sages said¹⁷</t>
    <t s="7">on the verse “When a man’s wife goes astray,”</t>
    <t s="8">“A person does not commit a transgression unless a spirit of folly enters into him.”</t>
    <t s="9">For a Jewish person, from his own essence</t>
    <t s="10">(a Jew from his own essence),</t>
    <t s="11">it is absolutely impossible to commit any transgression, as is stated in the Zohar,</t>
    <t s="12">on the verse,¹⁸</t>
    <t s="13">“When a soul [nefesh] will sin”—the Torah and the Holy One, blessed be He, wonder about it and say, “When a soul will sin”</t>
    <t s="14">(in astonishment).</t>
    <t s="15">And this means that even at the level of nefesh,¹⁹</t>
    <t s="16">which is not the essence of the soul,</t>
    <t s="17">and moreover, even among the five names by which the soul is called,</t>
    <t s="18">it is the lowest level among the names,</t>
    <t s="19">and as the Zohar there precisely states that the matter of sin applies specifically to nefesh,</t>
    <t s="20">for at the level of neshamah and even at the level of ruach, sin cannot apply,</t>
    <t s="21">nevertheless, even if at this level there would be a sin, it says about this “wonder.”</t>
    <t s="22">And moreover, even if it is only unintentional,</t>
    <t s="23">for the verse speaks about the matter of an unintentional sin,</t>
    <t s="24">behold, this too cannot be except through the spirit of folly that enters him.</t>
    <t s="25">For from his own essence,</t>
    <t s="26">behold, it is the nature of every Jew that he does not want and is unable to be separated from G‑dliness.²⁰</t>
    <t s="27">Rather, through the spirit of folly that covers the truth, and it seems to him that even when he commits a transgression he is still in his Judaism,</t>
    <t s="28">from this it is possible for him to commit a transgression.</t>
    <t s="29">But when the truth shines upon him,</t>
    <t s="30">the aspect of “And the truth of Hashem is forever,”²¹</t>
    <t s="31">then he feels that through the transgression, even a Rabbinic prohibition or a minor stringency of the words of the Scribes, he is utterly separated from G‑dliness,</t>
    <t s="32">even more than the shells and the sitra achra.</t>
    <t s="33">And as stated by the Alter Rebbe in Tanya,</t>
    <t s="34">that a person who transgresses His will, may He be blessed, is worse and lower than unclean animals, etc., which do not change their function.²²</t>
    <t s="35">And although he himself does not see, his mazal sees.²³</t>
    <t s="36">Therefore, a person from whom the Divine image has not departed from his face, they do not have dominion over him,</t>
    <t s="37">for “His charge, may He be blessed, guards their spirit.”²⁴</t>
    <t s="38">And as it is stated,²⁵</t>
    <t s="39">“And your fear and your dread shall be upon every beast of the earth,”</t>
    <t s="40">and only in one in whom “in our image, after our likeness”²⁶ is not apparent</t>
    <t s="41">do they have dominion, etc.</t>
    <t s="42">And similarly, the nations of the world and the shells and the sitra achra do not transgress His will, may He be blessed,</t>
    <t s="43">rather they call Him “G‑d of the gods,”²⁷</t>
    <t s="44">for they say that they too have dominion and rule,</t>
    <t s="45">but nevertheless they do not rebel against Him, may He be blessed,²⁸</t>
    <t s="46">for they call Him “G‑d of the gods,”</t>
    <t s="47">and they never transgress His will, may He be blessed.</t>
    <t s="48">And a person who commits a transgression, who rebels against His will, may He be blessed, is worse than the shells and the sitra achra and the things influenced by them, which are unclean animals and wild beasts,</t>
    <t s="49">to the extent that even a mosquito,</t>
    <t s="50">which takes in but does not expel,²⁹</t>
    <t s="51">precedes you.³⁰</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
